import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-! # The Poincaré Conjecture

References:
- [Miln2022](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/poincare.pdf)
- [Wang2017](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2017/186-2/p03).
- [mo296171](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/296171/unique-smooth-structure-on-3-manifolds)
- [mathlib4](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4)

The formalisations in this file are based on the ones written by Junyan Xu in Mathlib4.
-/

namespace PoincareConjecture

open scoped Manifold ContDiff EuclideanGeometry ContinuousMap

local macro:max "𝕊" noWs n:superscript(term) : term =>
  `(Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin ($(⟨n.raw[0]⟩) + 1))) 1)

/-- The predicate that the generalized Poincaré conjecture holds in dimension $n$, i.e. that
any $n$-dimensional manifold that is homotopy equivalent to the sphere is in fact homeomorphic
to the sphere. -/
def ConjectureFor (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Type) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [ChartedSpace (ℝ^n) M], M ≃ₕ 𝕊ⁿ → Nonempty (M ≃ₜ 𝕊ⁿ)

/--
The Millennium Problem, solved by Grigori Perelman in 2003: the Poincaré Conjecture holds.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture : ConjectureFor 3 := by
  sorry

/--
The Generalized Poincaré Conjecture holds for surfaces.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.dimension_two : ConjectureFor 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The Generalized Poincaré Conjecture holds for dimensions at least 5.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.dimension_ge_five (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) : ConjectureFor n := by
  sorry

/--
The Generalized Poincaré Conjecture holds in dimension 4.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.dimension_four : ConjectureFor 4 := by
  sorry

/-- The predicate that the smooth Poincaré conjecture holds in dimension $n$. -/
def SmoothConjectureFor (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Type) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (ℝ^n) M] [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M],
    M ≃ₕ 𝕊ⁿ → Nonempty (M ≃ₘ⟮𝓡 n, 𝓡 n⟯ 𝕊ⁿ)

/-- A reformulation of the Millennium Problem in terms of smooth 3-folds. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_for_three : SmoothConjectureFor 3 := by
  sorry

/-- The smooth formulation of the Millennium Problem implies the general case. This follows from
the fact that every topological 3-fold admits a smooth structure [mo296171]. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_implication (H : SmoothConjectureFor 3) :
    ConjectureFor 3 := by
  sorry

/-- The values at which the smooth version of the conjecture is known to hold. -/
def SmoothTrueValues : Set ℕ := {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 12, 56, 61}

/-- The smooth version of the Poincaré conjecture is known to hold in dimensions
$1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 12, 56, 61$. See [Wang2017]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_known_cases (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∈ SmoothTrueValues) :
    SmoothConjectureFor n := by
  sorry

/-- The four dimensional case of the smooth version of the conjecture is still open.
See [Wang2017]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_dimension_four : SmoothConjectureFor 4 := by
  sorry

/-- It is conjectured that the only values of $n > 4$ for which the smooth version of the
conjecture holds are $n = 5, 6, 12, 56, 61$. See Conjecture 1.17 in [Wang2017]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 54 57]
theorem poincare_conjecture.variants.smooth_other_cases (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 4)
    (hn' : n ∉ SmoothTrueValues) : ¬ SmoothConjectureFor n := by
  sorry

end PoincareConjecture

findings.description: The quantifiers at lines 72–74 omit `[T2Space M]`. Neither `ChartedSpace` nor `IsManifold` supplies Hausdorffness: they impose local charts and smooth coordinate changes only. Homotopy equivalence to the sphere does not repair this omission. For any n ≥ 1, take an open unit ball B in stereographic coordinates on S^n and glue an extra copy of B to S^n along A = {x ∈ B | x₁ < 0}. The resulting M has a smooth n-dimensional atlas, but the two copies of the origin are inseparable, so M cannot be diffeomorphic to S^n. Nevertheless M is homotopy equivalent to S^n. There is a retraction r collapsing the extra ball onto its original copy. The affine isotopy F_t(x) = (1 − 3t/4)x − (3t/8)e₁ preserves B and A and sends all of B into A at t = 1; it extends over the sphere by fixing infinity. Applying it on both pieces, then reversing it inside the original sphere, gives id_M homotopic to i ∘ r, while r ∘ i = id. Thus the present predicate is false in every positive dimension, rather than expressing the smooth Poincaré conjecture. This affects `smooth_for_three`, `smooth_known_cases`, and `smooth_dimension_four`; it also makes the premise of `smooth_implication` unsatisfiable and allows `smooth_other_cases` to hold for reasons unrelated to exotic spheres.
findings.source_evidence: Wang–Xu, Annals of Mathematics 186 (2017), introduction, Question 1.4: “Let M be a closed n-manifold. Suppose M is homeomorphic to S^n. Is M diffeomorphic to S^n?” Conjecture 1.17 concerns unique smooth structures on S^5, S^6, S^12, S^56, and S^61, not non-Hausdorff spaces merely homotopy equivalent to spheres. https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v186-n2-p03-p.pdf. Milnor’s Clay description, p. 5, likewise asks whether every smooth homotopy 4-sphere is diffeomorphic to S^4. The distinction is explicit in Mathlib’s `ChartedSpace.t1Space` documentation, which warns that charted spaces need not be T2.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `[T2Space M]` immediately after `[TopologicalSpace M]` in `SmoothConjectureFor`, matching `ConjectureFor`. With Hausdorffness, the homotopy-sphere hypothesis forces compactness, and compactness supplies second countability, so those extra assumptions are not necessary. Alternatively, using a homeomorphism-to-the-sphere premise would directly match Wang–Xu’s formulation and imply these topological properties.

reformulations.difference: The source quantifies over closed n-manifolds; Lean quantifies over Hausdorff spaces charted on ℝ^n without explicitly requiring compactness or second countability.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 1, a homotopy equivalence M ≃ S^n makes M connected and gives nonzero H_n(M; ℤ/2). Hatcher’s Proposition 3.29 says that a connected noncompact Hausdorff n-manifold has zero homology in degrees ≥ n; his manifold definition does not assume second countability. Consequently M must be compact. A finite subcover of Euclidean charts then gives second countability. The ℝ^n model already excludes boundary. For n = 0, charted spaces are discrete, and homotopy equivalence to the two-point sphere is a homeomorphism, hence also forces compactness. Thus the omitted restrictions follow from the actual premises.

reformulations.difference: The Millennium problem is stated using a simply connected closed 3-manifold, whereas Lean uses homotopy equivalence to S^3 through `ConjectureFor 3`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The Lean hypotheses imply compactness as above and simple connectivity by homotopy invariance. Conversely, a simply connected closed 3-manifold is orientable and has the integral homology of S^3 by Poincaré duality. Hurewicz and Whitehead then give a homotopy equivalence with S^3. Wang–Xu explicitly record this equivalence immediately after Conjecture 1.1. Hence this is a standard equivalent formulation, not a stronger homotopy hypothesis that loses cases.

review.notes: One underlying definition defect is reported once rather than duplicated across its five dependent smooth variants. The dimension list and the n > 4 exclusion match the cited source, and no independent status mismatch was found. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` and `/workspace/review/boundary.lean` compile without errors; they check the relevant classes, sphere instances, empty-type exclusion, both zero-dimensional predicates, set membership and bounds, the proposed correction, and the Hausdorff consequence of a diffeomorphism. The full non-Hausdorff gluing counterexample is explained in `/workspace/review/counterexample.md`; its complete construction is not proved in Lean. All review artifacts are outside the checkout, and the target file was left unchanged.

submission.summary: Added `[T2Space M]` to `SmoothConjectureFor`, excluding non-Hausdorff counterexamples and correcting the scope of its dependent smooth variants. No other declarations were edited. The requested compile command succeeds with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
